basis: Infantile multisystem autoimmunity with diabetes 2/2; intellectual disability and seizures 1/2 support neurologic involvement. Airway findings do not establish direct autoimmune injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: asthma and bronchiolitis each reported in 1/2, but neither establishes direct pulmonary damage from the autoimmune syndrome.

basis: Cobalamin metabolic defect with defining anemia and neurodevelopmental impairment; cardiac malformations 30-79% by HPO. Stomatitis 4/12 omitted by four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay, intellectual disability and seizures explicitly characterize the disease in its definition.

basis: Central autonomic hypoventilation and intestinal aganglionosis define syndrome; strabismus in 80-99% represents ocular alignment dysfunction. Hypoventilation does not establish lung injury.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus in 80-99% represents impaired ocular alignment and binocular function, supporting functional ocular involvement.

basis: Intrinsic phagocyte oxidative-burst defect; CGD-associated granulomatous colitis occurs in 4/8. Pulmonary fibrosis is 1/8; infections alone do not establish direct lung involvement.

decisions.haematologic: primary: defective neutrophil oxidative burst is an intrinsic blood-cell functional disorder, documented in 3/3, alongside immunodeficiency.

basis: Human poisoning predominantly follows ingestion, directly injuring gastrointestinal mucosa. Lung and injection-site injury depend on uncommon exposure routes; systemic organ failure is variable.

decisions.pulmonary: none: direct lung injury characterizes inhalational exposure, an uncommon route accounting for well under 30% of typical human cases.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency with intrinsic leukocyte dysfunction and cytopenias. Bronchiectasis 1/3 and reported fibrosis are secondary infectious sequelae, not established direct immune lung injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis 1/3 reaches the frequency threshold but is a separately diagnosed infectious sequel; direct intrinsic pulmonary damage is not established.

basis: Intellectual disability defines disease. Pes planus 3/4 lacks documented functional damage; hearing loss 1/4 is below threshold. Incontinence alone does not establish urinary tract injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes planus in 3/4 establishes common foot morphology, but no damaging deformity or musculoskeletal functional loss is documented.

basis: Autoinflammatory syndrome with diagnostic peritonitis and arthritis (5/5); pleuritis occurs in 4/5. Renal amyloidosis (2/5) is a separate secondary disease; rash is transient.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: recurrent inflammatory peritonitis is a major diagnostic criterion of familial Mediterranean fever.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: recurrent arthritis is a major diagnostic criterion, supported here by polyarticular arthritis in 5/5.

basis: Nasopharyngeal inflammation affects the pulmonary airway axis; most cases are infectious, including the common cold and infectious adenoiditis.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: infection accounts for most nasopharyngitis across this umbrella, although the anatomical definition does not specify an organism.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining leukoencephalopathy and developmental impairment in 7/7; optic pallor and visual impairment in 5/7. Weakness does not establish intrinsic myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: primary: leukoencephalopathy and neurodevelopmental impairment define the clinical syndrome, with white-matter abnormalities and intellectual disability in 7/7.
